title: Rocket Lab Corporation — Consensus Investment Report
subtitle: A structured debate between five independent investment frameworks — Buffett owner-earnings value, Munger multidisciplinary quality, Damodaran fundamental valuation, Druckenmiller macro-first expectations, and Soros reflexivity — reconciled into a single synthesized analysis and recommendation.

exec_summary.lead: Rocket Lab is an exceptional, founder-run, vertically integrated space company — one of only two self-launching space powers on earth — with a real moat, a record **$2.36B** backlog, and extraordinary growth optionality in Neutron and Iridium. Five independent analyses — using five different frameworks — each refused to buy at **$80.25** and converged on the **same rating: C — Hold/Watch**. The business is not in dispute; the price, the binary Neutron/Iridium catalysts, and the equity-funded growth model are. The fundamental lenses value the equity at ~$6–16 (5–13× below price); the macro lenses see a balanced ~+11–12% 12-month price path.

profiles_title: The Five Positions at the Table
profiles_lead: Each participant analyzed Rocket Lab independently. Their positions were then cross-examined in the debate.

profiles.name: Warren Buffett
profiles.paragraph: Three-scenario DCF: bear **~$6**, base **~$15**, bull **~$26**, weighted **~$14**. The stock trades at ~62× trailing sales — roughly **5–6× my base-case intrinsic value** — and TTM FCF is **−$371M**: zero owner earnings. "Great company, terrible entry price. Price is what you pay, value is what you get." **Rating: C — Watch; I become interested only below ~$10.**

profiles.name: Charlie Munger
profiles.paragraph: Conservative DCF (21.7% discount = WACC+3%, 0–2% terminal growth): bear **$3.44**, base **$6.12**, bull **$8.38**, weighted **$5.63**. Even my bull case is worth less than a tenth of the $80.25 price. "The market is not pricing the business; it is pricing a lottery ticket on Neutron and Iridium." **Rating: D — Avoid; buy only below ~$20.**

profiles.name: Aswath Damodaran
profiles.paragraph: SBC-aware FCFF DCF (12% WACC, 3% terminal growth, ROIC 10%→18%): base **$11.00**; probability-weighted **$16.82** across five scenarios (severe bear **$4.91** / bear **$5.94** / bull **$25.09** / extreme bull **$50.22**). At $80.25 that is **−79.04% expected upside** and **−26.84% 5-year annualized** — a reverse DCF requires a "second SpaceX" outcome. Value emerges only below ~$25–30; conviction <$20. **Rating: D — Avoid / Significantly Overvalued.**

profiles.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
profiles.paragraph: Probability-weighted **~+12% expected 12-month return (~$90)** with **~1.8:1 asymmetry** — positive, not exceptional. The macro is a headwind (10Y ~4.69%, hawkish Fed hold, energy shock) and the defining catalyst (Neutron first flight, end-2026) is binary and months out. Get aggressive on confirmation (Neutron on the pad/first-flight success, 10Y <~4.3%) or a dislocation to **$50–65**.

profiles.name: George Soros
profiles.paragraph: A reflexive machine whose price funds its own growth (Q2'26 **$1.08B ATM**); the trend is real, the perception partially wrong (timeline + ~62× sales). Scenarios: bear **$58** / base **$88** / bull **$115** / extreme bull **$135** / extreme bear **$40**, weighted ≈**$89** (+11%), asymmetry **~1.1×** — fair, not exceptional. Attractive only after a dislocation into **$62–72** or a confirmed positive binary.

debate.title: The Debate: Agreement, Contention, Resolution
debate.lead: Round 1: opening statements. Round 2: uncontested common ground. Round 3: six disputed points, cross-examined to resolution. Round 4: final concessions.
agreements: **This is an exceptional, real business.** Founder-run, vertically integrated — one of only two self-launching space powers on earth; real moat (flight heritage, private Mahia pad + US–NZ treaty, vertical integration, Iridium's scarce L-band spectrum); record Q2'26 revenue ($234M, +62% y/y); **$2.36B** record backlog (45.5% converts in 12 months).
**The business is not in dispute; the price is.** No profile buys at $80.25; no profile recommends a short. Five frameworks, five refusals at the current price.

**Neutron is THE swing factor.** Unflown, slipped ~five times, Stage-1 tank ruptured January 2026, "window narrowing"; ~14% probability of a 2026 launch (prediction markets). A successful first flight re-rates the entire story; a static-fire/first-flight failure flips the narrative from "when" to "if."

**Iridium is transformative but risky.** $8.0B EV ($54/share cash+stock), funded by a **$3.6B committed bridge** plus assumption of Iridium's **$1.775B term loan**; close mid-2027; financing and integration unbuilt; converts a net-cash fortress into a levered balance sheet.

**Valuation is extreme.** 62× TTM sales / ~42× forward with no GAAP earnings through FY27 (consensus adj EPS −$0.05 FY26 / +$0.05 FY27); the price embeds a "second SpaceX" outcome the cash-flow math does not support.

**Dilution is structural.** Shares +15.7% YoY (598.5M → ~641M guided); $1.08B ATM Q2'26 plus $1.12B FY25; $3.0B ATM authorization; 141.8M shares reserved (~24% overhang); evergreen plan +5%/yr. Growth is funded by shareholders, not by the business.

**The cash bridge is real but finite.** Net cash ~$2.25B ($3.77/share) cushions a TTM FCF of **−$371M**; management guides adjusted-EBITDA-positive the quarter after a successful first Neutron flight and FCF-positive 18–24 months later.

**The single valuation-critical variable is the FCF/EBITDA inflection after Neutron's first successful flight** — the hinge that reconciles the fundamental lenses (IV ~$6–16) with the macro lenses (12-mo price ~$88–103). If Neutron flies and the P&L inflects, the equity-funded reinvestment turns value-creating; if it fails or slips, value converges toward net cash.

**The macro is a headwind.** 10Y ~4.69% near its 52-week high, a hawkish Fed hold under Chair Warsh with three dissents for a hike, and an energy-driven inflation shock — a discount-rate headwind for a 2.63-beta, long-duration, cash-burning growth stock.
debate.contentions_title: Contested points — and how they were resolved
contentions: **Reference price: intrinsic value vs 12-month price (the fundamental-vs-macro split).** Buffett/Munger/Damodaran frame scenario values as **intrinsic value today** (~$6–16; price 5–13× IV); Druckenmiller/Soros frame them as **12-month price expectations** (~$88–103). Cross-examination: Soros to the IV camp — "your $11–16 tells me nothing about the next quarter; the stock can run to $95 on a Neutron flight." Buffett to the price-path camp — "your $88–103 base is the consensus price target — the market's belief, not a mispricing." **Named concession:** Druckenmiller and Soros concede their cells are 12-month price paths, not IV ("on an IV basis I am as bearish as the fundamental lenses"). **Resolved:** the three IV models set the consensus IV; Druckenmiller/Soros inform the near-term ladder and triggers. Both frames converge: **do not initiate at $80.25.**

**Where does base-case intrinsic value actually sit?** Buffett ~$15 (moderate discount), Munger $6.12 (21.7% discount, 0–2% terminal growth — "demand a penalty"), Damodaran **$11.00** (verified workbook: 12% WACC, 3% terminal growth, SBC-aware margins, ROIC 10%→18%). Cross-examination: Munger to Buffett — "a 2.63-beta cash-burning business does not deserve your discount rate." Buffett concedes the discount-rate spread is the entire difference and publishes $6–26 as the range. **Resolved:** consensus base ≈ **~$11** (the workbook anchor); Buffett's ~$15 is the optimistic fundamental read, Munger's ~$6 the conservative. It sits ~86% below the price — the fundamental-vs-macro chasm made concrete.

**How much credit for the right tail (Neutron + Iridium)?** Fundamental IV: Damodaran bull **$25.09** / extreme bull **$50.22** (25%/10%); Buffett ~$26; Munger $8.38. Macro 12-mo price paths: Druckenmiller bull $135 (+68%); Soros bull $115 (+43%) / extreme bull $135 (+68%). Cross-examination: Damodaran to the macro camp — "your $135 is the consensus price target; my extreme-bull IV of **$50.22** is what the business is *worth* even if every catalyst lands, and it is **−37% below today's price**." Druckenmiller — "the market trades the binary; if Neutron flies, the stock re-rates toward $95+ before your IV catches up." **Named concession:** Druckenmiller concedes the tail is "real but already partially in the price"; Soros concedes it needs *both* Neutron *and* Iridium — "if one fails, the compound narrative breaks." **Resolved:** the right tail justifies watching and precludes a short, but does not justify buying at $80.25 — the market is paying for the price-path tail, not the value tail.

**What price compensates for the uncertainty?** Fundamental buy zones <$10–30 (Buffett <$10; Munger <$20; Damodaran ≤$30 first tranche, <$20 conviction); macro buy zones $50–72 (Druckenmiller $50–65 dislocation; Soros $62–72). Cross-examination: Buffett to Soros — "you'd buy at $62–72, 4–5× my base-case IV — where is your margin of safety?" Soros — "I buy a 12-month reflexive position with defined stops, cushioned by $3.77/share net cash and a $2.36B backlog; different games, same name." **Named concessions:** Druckenmiller concedes $50–65 is a trading/dislocation zone requiring confirmation (10Y <~4.3%); Soros concedes $62–72 is tactical at only ~1.1–1.3×; Damodaran/Munger concede a successful Neutron de-risks value toward the $20–30 first-tranche zone. **Resolved (unanimous):** composite ladder — tactical starter **$62–72**, tactical accumulate **$50–62**, fundamental accumulate **$20–30**, high-conviction **<$20**, hard do-not-initiate at $80.25. The dispute is about sizing, temperament, and horizon — nobody buys at $80.25.

**Management quality & the dilution / insider-selling question.** Buffett ~7/10 (world-class founder-execution; austere comp $6.83M, 88:1 pay ratio, forfeited RSUs, candid); Munger ~5–6/10 ("a CFO who realized **$86M** while the company lost **$198M** — the incentive picture is poisoned by structure"); Damodaran ~7/10 ("Excellent operationally, Good on capital allocation — but equity-funded growth pushes risk onto shareholders"); Soros ~6/10 (insider selling ~$300M+ into the drawdown). Cross-examination: Munger — "the dilution treadmill is the incentive problem in one data point." Buffett — "the equity raises fund exactly the growth the bulls demand, and Beck personally paid in forgone comp." **Named concessions:** Buffett concedes the dilution is real (+15.7% shares YoY, ~24% overhang); Soros concedes Beck's comp is austere but the cycle-low concentration remains a caution flag; Munger concedes Beck is an honest, superb founder — the dispute is the structure, not the man. **Resolved:** consensus management **6/10** — docked for dilution, the $8B Iridium leverage, and insider selling.

**Is 62× trailing sales / no earnings / negative FCF a red flag or a growth-stage artifact?** The bear reading (Munger, Damodaran): ROIC **−5.5% < WACC 12%**; OCF (−$222M) worse than the net loss (−$165M); working capital consumed ~$136M in H1'26; no owner earnings. The counter-reading (Buffett, partially Druckenmiller): high-quality organic growth (space systems +38.6% QoQ, cost per launch −31%, GM 21%→37%, record backlog) — a pre-profit hyper-grower with a real inflection path. Cross-examination: Damodaran to Buffett — "OCF − capex − SBC ≈ **−$393M** of economic cash consumption in FY25, funded entirely by ATM raises; the growth is real, the *funding* is the risk." **Named concession:** Druckenmiller concedes there is **no cash-flow valuation floor today** — "the market will not reward earnings until Neutron de-risks the P&L."; Damodaran concedes the growth is genuinely organic and margins are inflecting on the gross line. **Resolved:** a **real fragility, not an artifact** — it is why the fundamental IV sits so far below the price, why no margin of safety exists at $80.25, and why the FCF/EBITDA inflection is the valuation-critical variable.

The consensus weighted value **converges exactly on Damodaran's verified workbook value ($16.82)**; the three fundamental weighted values span **$5.63 (Munger) → ~$14 (Buffett) → $16.82 (Damodaran)** — a simple midpoint (~$12) is a reasonable low-end read. Aggressive and, at the value level, unreachable by the fundamental math.

conclusions.title: The Five Consensus Conclusions
items: **The Business.** Rocket Lab is an exceptional, founder-run, vertically integrated space company — one of only two "self-launching" space powers on earth (build, launch, operate its own satellites) — with a real moat (flight heritage, private NZ pad + US–NZ treaty, vertical integration, Iridium's scarce L-band spectrum), a record $2.36B backlog, and extraordinary growth optionality in Neutron and Iridium. The business quality is not in dispute; the price is.

**The Economics.** The sole determinant of long-term per-share value is **the FCF/EBITDA inflection after Neutron's first successful flight** — whether an unflown medium-lift rocket and a levered $8B acquisition convert the equity-funded reinvestment (ROIC −5.5% vs ~12% WACC) into positive free cash flow inside a credible window. If Neutron flies and the P&L inflects, growth turns value-creating; if it fails or slips, value converges toward net cash (~$3.77/share) and the backlog. The per-share tax is dilution (shares +15.7% YoY, ~24% issuance overhang), not interest.

**The Market's Expectations.** At $80.25 the market is implicitly assuming a successful Neutron first launch, an accretive Iridium close, ~40%+ revenue growth for years, a 10-year that does not break out to 5%+, and no further heavy dilution — a "second SpaceX" outcome requiring ~$25–30B terminal revenue at 22–25% operating margins, at ~5× the consensus weighted IV and 62× trailing sales / ~42× forward. Aggressive but not impossible; the consensus "Buy / $112.94 PT" reflects it. The Street's uniformity is itself a risk if Neutron slips.

**The Valuation.** Consensus base intrinsic value **~$11/share**; probability-weighted **~$16.82/share** (verified workbook anchor); bear **~$5–7**; bull **~$25**; extreme bull **~$50** (Damodaran workbook: $4.91 / $5.94 / $11.00 / $25.09 / $50.22, weighted $16.82, upside −79.04%, 5-yr annualized −26.84%). Confidence: **Low/Medium** — the direction of overvaluation is robust (the entire fundamental distribution sits below the price), the magnitude is uncertain (the Neutron/Iridium binary). The 12-month price-path lenses (Druckenmiller ~$90, Soros ≈$89, +11–12%) are balanced-to-positive but not exceptional (~1.1×–1.8× asymmetry). Both the base and weighted fundamental values are far below the $80.25 price — expected upside ≈ −79%, 5-year annualized ≈ −27%.

**The Investment Decision.** **C — Hold/Watch at ~$80.25; do not initiate above ~$72.** Tactical starter **$62–72** (Soros), tactical accumulate **$50–62** (Druckenmiller, on dislocation + confirmation), fundamental accumulate **$20–30**, high-conviction **<$20** (Damodaran/Munger conviction; Buffett <$10), provided the monitoring hierarchy (Neutron first-flight status > FCF/EBITDA inflection > Iridium close & financing > dilution/share count > backlog & margin) stays intact. Upgrades require proof — a successful Neutron first flight, a confirmed FCF inflection, a low-dilution Iridium close, and/or a margin of safety — and a 10Y roll below ~4.3%. The binary catalyst and the operating data, not the stock price, will deliver the verdict.

judgment.title: Final Consensus Judgment
judgment.paragraph: At a price of **$80.25**, the market is paying ~62× trailing sales — about **five times the consensus probability-weighted intrinsic value of $16.82** and roughly seven times the ~$11 base — for a company that has produced **zero owner earnings** in its history (TTM FCF −$371M) and whose entire valuation rests on an **unflown medium-lift rocket (Neutron)** and a **levered $8B acquisition (Iridium)** landing roughly simultaneously. Five independent frameworks — owner-earnings value, multidisciplinary quality, fundamental DCF, macro/liquidity-driven expectations, and reflexivity — all refuse to buy at this price, all land on a **C (Hold/Watch, or Monitor)** at the unified margin (with Munger and Damodaran recording **D — Avoid** as their intrinsic-value verdict), and all place the valuation-critical variable on the same hinge: **whether Neutron's first successful flight converts the equity-funded reinvestment into positive free cash flow inside a credible window, and whether dilution and the Iridium financing allow per-share value to compound at anything like the rate the price assumes.** We agree the business is exceptional, Neutron and Iridium are real but binary, the balance sheet is a fortress today but will be levered by Iridium, dilution is structural, the macro is a headwind, and the valuation embeds a "second SpaceX" outcome with no margin of safety and no earnings floor. The most dangerous risks are a **Neutron static-fire/first-flight failure** (which flips the narrative to "if" and compresses the multiple hard), **another Neutron slip into 2027**, a **dilution-heavy Iridium financing or deal break**, a **sustained cash burn without an inflection path**, and a **10-year regime shift above ~5%** on a 2.63-beta multiple with no cash-flow floor. Therefore, at today's price the consensus is to **hold and wait**: do not initiate above ~$72; take a tactical starter at **$62–72**, a tactical accumulate at **$50–62** (on dislocation and confirmation), a fundamental accumulate at **$20–30**, and high-conviction only **below $20**; and let the Neutron flight, the FCF inflection, the Iridium close, and the share count — not the "space power" narrative — decide whether this exceptional company becomes an exceptional investment.

Damodaran's scenario values are the verified `RKLB_Damodaran_Financial_Model.xlsx` workbook outputs (verifier: ALL_MATCH): Severe Bear $4.91 / Bear $5.94 / Base $11.00 / Bull $25.09 / Extreme Bull $50.22, probability-weighted $16.82, upside −79.04%, 5-yr annualized −26.84% (WACC 12.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, probabilities 0.10/0.20/0.35/0.25/0.10). This document is an educational synthesis of estimates about estimates — it is **not investment advice**, and no valuation herein should be treated as a price prediction or a recommendation to trade.
